_readme: Persistent fetch-failure ledger for the Las Azules S2 media sweep routine. Sweeps must read this before attempting any body fetch on a candidate URL and skip anything currently in cooldown, rendering the skip on the sweep evidence line. failCount tracks consecutive full fallback-chain failures (WebFetch AND Firecrawl scrape both failed in the same attempt). Three consecutive full-chain failures sets cooldownUntil to 30 days out. After cooldown expires, the URL gets one retry (WebFetch then Firecrawl); success resets failCount to 0 and clears cooldownUntil, failure restarts the 30-day cooldown. A separate category, permanentSkip with a skipReason, marks URLs that are fetchable but excluded for an editorial reason (for example a syndicated republication of a story already in data.json under a primary outlet). permanentSkip entries are skipped regardless of cooldownUntil and must never be treated as, or logged as, a fetch failure. See LEMA-9620 for origin, LEMA-9619 for the incident that motivated this file, and LEMA-9621 for the permanentSkip category. Two standing editorial rules, adopted LEMA-9642 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9641), apply to every sweep going forward and must not be re-escalated: (1) No proxy, inferred, or approximated dates ever enter data.json. A crawler artifact like this ledger's firstSeen timestamp is never a substitute for a real, sourced publish date -- not even with a disclaimer in the excerpt, because sorting and the dashboard KPIs read ts, not the excerpt. If no real publish date can be recovered (WebFetch AND Firecrawl both exhausted), the candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_undateable" and reviewable: true, never added with a substitute date. (2) Social-candidate relevance gate, separate from and prior to any dateability check: vendor, supplier, crew-personal, and fan-repost accounts are not media coverage and must be skipped as permanentSkip on relevance grounds (skipReason "editorial_vendor_promo" for a vendor/supplier company account, "editorial_personal_repost" for an individual crew-personal or fan-repost account) regardless of whether a date could be found. Publisher, outlet, and editorial-brand accounts are media coverage and are evaluated normally, dateability included. reviewable: true (used on editorial_undateable entries only) marks a permanentSkip entry as genuine coverage omitted solely for lack of a real date, distinct from editorial_redundant_syndication (we already have the story) and editorial_vendor_promo/editorial_personal_repost (not coverage at all, dateability irrelevant). It is queryable only, for a future manual date lookup; it implies no dashboard or UI surfacing.

entries.skipNote: Mandatory date-recovery gate (LEMA-9642, CEO ruling on LEMA-9641): prior six attempts (see history) all used WebFetch only, because the fallback chain fires only on failure and WebFetch kept returning 200 with real content. WebFetch summarizes the body and does not surface timestamp elements. On 2026-09-03 a targeted Firecrawl scrape was attempted, explicitly to check og:article:published_time, datePublished, and the rendered post timestamp: Firecrawl returned success:false, "we do not support this site" -- a blanket policy refusal for facebook.com, not a per-URL technical failure (consistent with the 403s Firecrawl has returned against every other facebook.com URL in this ledger). As supplementary diligence beyond the mandated Firecrawl attempt, the raw page HTML was also fetched directly and searched for date-bearing meta tags and JSON fields: og:type, og:description, og:image, og:url, og:locale are present, but no og:article:published_time, datePublished, publish_time, creation_time, or any other publish/creation timestamp field exists anywhere in the ~466KB page source. The only time-like values present are client-side request-timing telemetry (timeOfRequestStart/timeOfResponseStart), not a publication date. Both WebFetch and Firecrawl are now exhausted and no date is recoverable from the fetchable page. Per Ruling 1 (LEMA-9641), no proxy or approximated date may be substituted. Skipped as editorial_undateable, reviewable=true so this entry stays listable for a future manual date lookup (e.g. if a news pickup ever cites this post's exact date).
